newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst, Clariant merge specialty chemicals.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst, Clariant merge specialty chemicals.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG said on Tuesday it will merge its specialty chemicals business with Swiss group Clariant AG, in a bid to overcome conditions in the business sector.

Hoechst said it will take a sizeable minority stake in Clariant, adding the new merged specialty chemicals group will post annual sales of nine billion marks. In a statement Hoechst said the step reflects the difficult situation in its own specialty chemicals unit.

Hoechst said it will contribute its speciality chemicals business, masterbatches, which are tailored plastic resins, pigments and additives and auxilliaries including textile and leather chemicals, fine chemicals, dispersions and cellulose ethers into the new group.
A Hoechst spokeswoman said the group's supervisory board had not yet agreed to the merger but expected to receive an answer from the board this afternoon.

Hoechst said Clariant would remain a Swiss share company, indicating that Hoechst would effectively receive a share market quotation for these products and thus increase shareholder value for the parent company.

The merger will result in a larger product portfolio as well as an improved geographical presence and new growth opportunities. Both companies look to gain savings totalling several hundred million Swiss francs from the deal.
